lines: +# Rescue experiment — what was wrong and what I changed
+Three bugs, all in our tree (`/root/miles/examples/sql_agent/rescue/`). The launcher
+recipe is untouched, including `--pause-generation-mode in_place`; no Miles/SGLang
+files were modified. Regression tests: `tests/fast/examples/test_sql_agent_rescue.py`.
+## 1. The projection sampler was not sampling from the student (`projection.py`)
+The stated target is `p(x) ∝ pi(x | plain prompt) · 1[x passes]`, but the move
+acceptance was greedy hill-climbing on the *length-normalised* student log-prob
+(mean per policy token), with no proposal-ratio correction. That is not a sampler
+for the target: a long candidate full of predictable boilerplate beats a short,
+much more probable one (mean instead of sum), and trajectories that are only
+likely because the hint is in the prompt are kept (no correction for how much
+more likely the hinted proposal made them). Injected trajectories were therefore
+long, hint-shaped, and off the student's distribution (in a 12-step run: mean
+response length 1599 tokens, mean student log-prob sum ≈ −366, vs ≈ −252 after
+the fix at 1253 tokens).
+Fix: proper Metropolis–Hastings acceptance for the stated target,
+    log α = [S_π(x′) − S_π(x)] + [S_q(x suffix) − S_q(x′ suffix)] + log(T_x / T_x′)
+with `S` = summed log-probs over policy tokens (student `π`, hinted proposal
+`q` over the regenerated suffix only), `T` = turn counts for the uniform-cut
+ratio. See `mh_log_accept_ratio`.
+## 2. In-place weight pushes left stale KV/recurrent state in the engine (`rollout.py`)
+With `--pause-generation-mode in_place`, Miles skips the cache flush around the
+weight update (flushing would discard frozen requests' KV), and SGLang's prefix
+cache is keyed by token ids only — so after every push, the next rollout and
+eval reuse KV / linear-attention state computed under older weights (the
+~340-token system/tool prefix shared by every prompt keeps step-0 weights for
+the whole run). The trainer scores the same tokens with current weights, hence
+`train_rollout_kl` / `..._logprob_abs_diff` creeping as the weights move. I
+verified this standalone: after a no-flush weight update, re-scoring a fixed
+sequence on the warm cache vs after a flush differed by ~0.01–0.03/token.
+Fix: `RescueRolloutFn` now flushes the engine cache via the router at the start
+of every train *and* eval rollout (`flush_engine_cache`). In this synchronous
+recipe the engine is idle at that point, so the flush is safe; the in-place push
+itself is unchanged (production async carry-over is unaffected — in-flight
+requests there are a separate path, this flush only runs between sync steps).
+## 3. Student scores were taken from the warm-cache prefill path (`episode.py`)
+The sampler's student log-probs (used for accept/reject *and* written into the
+injected sample as `rollout_log_probs`) came from prefill scoring on a warm
+cache. On this hybrid linear-attention model the restored-recurrent-state path
+is measurably not a fresh forward: repeated scoring of a fixed sequence is
+bit-stable cold and on first reuse, then shifts by ~0.02/token on average
+(outliers > 1 nat), while a cold prefill matches generation log-probs to
+~0.001/token. Miles' own prefill log-prob recomputation flushes before scoring
+for the same reason. Summed over hundreds of tokens, the warm scores corrupted
+both the sampler's decisions and the TIS/KL bookkeeping of rescued samples.
+Fix: `EpisodeRunner.token_logprobs` flushes before scoring. A flush needs an
+idle engine, so rescue now processes groups sequentially instead of
+`asyncio.gather` (rescue time per step roughly 25–45 s, was ~15 s).
+## Verification (seed 1 unless noted)
+- Unit tests: 8 passed (MH acceptance cases that all failed before the fix,
+  MH ratio terms incl. tool-token masking, flush-before-generate/scoring,
+  sequential rescue). Existing prefill-logprobs suite also green.
+- 12-step runs: unfixed `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` slope ≈ +0.0014/step
+  (0.010 → 0.032); fixed ≈ +0.0004/step with a lower level, and rescued
+  trajectories shorter and at higher student density (above).
+- 50-step fixed run (`/app/runs/fixed50`): KL/abs-diff slopes ≈ 0 over the run
+  (abs-diff first-5 mean 0.0152, last-5 0.0193, slope −0.00005/step; levels
+  still batch-noisy because within-rollout prefix reuse is inherent to the
+  stock engine). Held-out pass@1 (n=2/prompt, noisy):
+- Caveat: this recipe has very high run-to-run variance (a plain-GRPO 50-step
+  control draw landed in a short-response regime and scored higher:
+  regular 0.66 / hard 0.20, while a 12-step plain draw was flat). Single-run
+  eval deltas of ±5 points are within noise; judge the fix by the sampler
+  distribution and the flat KL slope, and budget multiple seeds before
+  concluding rescue vs plain.
